hook.text: Hawaii sits in the middle of a tectonic plate, not at any boundary—so why is it volcanic?

buildup.text: A hotspot is a plume of hot mantle rising from deep inside Earth, melting through the plate above.

discovery.text: As the Pacific Plate moves northwest, the hotspot punches up new islands—creating a volcanic chain.

twist.text: The oldest Hawaiian island is 80 million years old—now submerged far northwest as a seamount.

climax.text: Hotspot chains record plate motion like a geological conveyor belt—direction and speed included.

punchline.text: The plate moves; the hotspot stays—leaving a trail of islands.

quiz.question: Why does Hawaii have volcanoes despite being mid-plate?
options: A mantle hotspot melts through the plate
